title: Italian Game: Fried Liver Attack
line: When Black takes back with the knight, White gives a knight on f7 and drags the king out.

steps.text: The Two Knights Defense: your knight went for f7, and Black blocked your bishop with a pawn.
Take the pawn. It blocked your bishop on its way to f7.
steps.after: This time the knight takes back, a slip common at club level. Masters move it to chase the bishop. Now only the king guards f7.

steps.text: Take on f7 with the knight. It attacks the queen and the rook, so the king has to take it.

also.d2d4: That is the Lolli Attack, also sound. This lesson takes on f7.

steps.after: Engines rate this sacrifice strong for White, and masters choose it. The king is out in the open.

steps.text: Check with the queen. It also attacks the knight on d5.
steps.hint: The queen gives check on the diagonal toward the king.

steps.text: The knight on d5 cannot move: it shields the king from your bishop. So the king steps up to guard it, into the middle of the board.
Bring another knight to attack the pinned knight. Now three of your pieces hit it.
steps.after: Black guards with the other knight, which also threatens to jump to c2 and attack your king and rook.

steps.text: Castle. Your king and rook leave before the knight can attack them both.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It opens the center while Black's king still stands in it.
steps.after: Black has a knight for two pawns, but its king is open and its pieces are tied up. That is what the sacrifice bought.

summary: Taking back with the knight leaves the weak pawn guarded by the king alone. A knight given there drags the king out.
